title: Relative differential sheaves: finite type and canonical cartesian base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:S'\to S$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Set $X'=X\times_S S'$, with projections $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^1_{X'/S'}$ be the relative differential sheaves with their universal derivations $d$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], and use ordinary module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. These differential sheaves are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. The canonical $\mathcal O_{X'}$-linear map $c_g:p^*\Omega^1_{X/S}\to\Omega^1_{X'/S'}$ characterized locally by $1\otimes da\mapsto d(p^\sharp a)$ is an isomorphism. For affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset S'$ with $f(U)\subset V$ and $g(V')\subset V$, put $A'=R'\otimes_R A$. On $U\times_V V'$ the map $c_g$ is the $A'$-linear isomorphism $A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/R}\to\Omega_{A'/R'}$, $b\otimes da\mapsto b\,d(1\otimes a)$, and these identifications agree on overlaps. If $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^1_{X'/S'}$ are of finite type as module sheaves [pqf-def-coherent]. No flatness or finite presentation is required.

proof.text: Construct the global map without gluing: compose the derivation on the second projection with the ring map of the first projection. The cartesian equation makes this a derivation relative to f. The universal property of relative differentials gives a map into the pushforward, and the section-normalized tensor-pullback adjunction transposes it to c. Applying these two bijections again proves the generator equation and uniqueness on every open.
Use the already proved source-library instance isQuasicoherent_relativeDifferentials for both morphisms. This instance uses the affine differential-sheaf description and local presentations.

Restrict the cartesian square to the affine triple U,V,V′. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.isPullback_resLE identifies the restricted fibre product with W=p^{-1}U intersect q^{-1}V′. The fibre product of affine schemes is affine. Mathlib isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen and isIso_pushoutSection_iff give the pushout of the four section rings with the actual appLE maps.

Apply the general proved affine tensor-pullback sections theorem to p and the quasi-coherent differential sheaf. Swap its tensor factors and transport from algebraic tensor products to ModuleCat.extendScalars; its second-factor linearity supplies linearity over the section ring of W. Compose with the affine differential-sections equivalence on U to obtain alpha with the specified unit formula. Apply the affine differential-sections theorem on W over V′ to obtain delta. Convert the section-ring pushout to Algebra.IsPushout and use Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquiv to obtain beta, including its formula on b tensor da.

Prove c_W composed with alpha equals delta composed with beta. The scalar-extension adjunction and the universal property of ring differentials reduce equality to tensors 1 tensor da. The normalization of alpha, naturality of c, the defining formula for c, and naturality of the target derivation give the equality. Thus all affine comparisons describe the same global morphism, and compatibility on overlaps follows from its naturality.

For each point of the global fibre product choose an affine base neighbourhood, an affine neighbourhood of its first projection over that base, and one of its second projection over the same base. Their W form a cover, including the empty case. The affine square expresses c_W as delta composed with beta composed with alpha inverse, hence it is bijective. Tensor pullback is quasi-coherent by comparison of left adjoints with ordinary pullback and the proved pullback quasi-coherence theorem. The affine-cover isomorphism criterion makes c an isomorphism.

For a locally finite type morphism choose an affine-pair cover. Its section ring maps are finite type, so Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.finite makes the ring differential modules finite, including zero rings and zero generators. Transport across relativeDifferentials_affine_sections and apply the affine finite-type criterion. Apply this argument to f and again to its base change q, which is locally finite type by stability under pullback.
